description: Terraluna finds places on Earth whose terrain resembles candidate Moon and Mars landing sites. A physics fingerprint, the structure function of 5 km elevation windows at 270 to 1080 m lags, compares NASA and ESA elevation models with Connecting Ridge, Jezero and Arcadia; for Jezero the best Earth window is 15x closer than the median. A self-supervised ResNet encoder (VICReg, physics head, planet adversary) runs in the browser via ONNX, beside a live finder and a 3D rover lab.
summary:
Terraluna finds places on Earth whose terrain matches candidate Moon and Mars landing sites, so astronauts and rover teams can choose analog training sites by measurement instead of experience alone.                

We built a physics terrain fingerprint: the structure function of 5 km elevation windows at 270 to 1080 m lags, which captures relief and texture. Computed from NASA lunar and Martian elevation models and Copernicus Earth elevation data, it compares Earth windows with Connecting Ridge at the lunar south pole, Jezero crater and Arcadia Planitia on Mars. For Jezero, the best Earth window is 15 times closer than the median window.

On top, we trained our own self-supervised terrain encoder: a ResNet with VICReg, a physics head and a gradient-reversal planet adversary, exported to ONNX and run directly in the browser. A web app brings it together: a live finder that measures any point on Earth in seconds, a 3D Lab where a rover drives the same route on real Earth and Mars terrain, evidence cards for every match, and a research paper with benchmarks.
details:
What it does

Terraluna answers one question: where on Earth does the ground look most like a Moon or Mars landing site? It compares terrain windows on Earth with three targets: Connecting Ridge (lunar south pole), Jezero crater and Arcadia Planitia (Mars), and reports the closest matches as evidence cards.

  

How it works

1. Physics terrain fingerprint: for every 5 km elevation window we compute the structure function nu(L), how much the height changes over distances from 270 m to 1080 m. This gives a relief and a texture fingerprint. Distances between fingerprints rank Earth windows against each target. The same code runs in Python and in TypeScript in the browser, verified by numerical parity tests.

2. Self-supervised terrain encoder: a ResNet-18-layout network (2.8M parameters, 256-d embedding) trained on 19,393 Moon, Mars and Earth windows with VICReg (two augmented views must agree), a physics head that predicts the fingerprint, and agradient-reversal adversary that pushes the model to ignore which planet a window comes from. It is exported to ONNX and runs in the browser on WebAssembly with a cosine agreement of 0.999995 to the training model. It is shown as an experimental second opinion next to the physics fingerprint.

3. Live finder: click any point on Earth. The browser fetches real Copernicus GLO-30 elevation, computes the fingerprint locally and compares it with the targets in seconds.

4. Lab: real elevation of an Earth site and a Mars or Moon target side by side in 3D at the same scale, with a simulated rover driving the same route on both and live slope, climb and descent statistics.

5. Evidence cards and paper: every match has a card with figures, distances and a proposed field test. A research paper documents the method, results and benchmarks.

  

Results

We searched 71 Earth windows per target in two regions (Holuhraun, Iceland and Rosamond Dry Lake, California). For Jezero crater the best Earth window is 15 times closer than the median window, for Arcadia Planitia 6 times. Training on a 

laptop GPU was about 34 times faster than on our CPU server.

  

Benefits and impact

Analog sites for astronaut and rover training are usually chosen by expert experience. Terraluna adds a reproducible, quantitative measure that works for any point on Earth, which helps plan field tests and lets more teams, students and researchers explore Moon and Mars analogs themselves.

  

Tools

Python (NumPy, PyTorch, ONNX), TypeScript, Next.js, React, three.js and react-three-fiber, shadcn/ui, Leaflet, ONNX Runtime Web (WebAssembly), Vercel, LaTeX. Training ran on a CPU server and an Apple laptop GPU (MPS).

  

Creativity and considerations

Terraluna measures terrain directly rather than relying on precomputed scores, so the same fingerprint works on the Moon, Mars and Earth, and it runs live in the browser. We kept every number traceable to recorded data, label evidence (derived, predicted) clearly, and keep the learned model separate from the physics ranking.
